Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

Bots inside your agent IDE.

Open source. Bring your own everything: your Claude Code or Codex, your local or remote machines, your tools. Ask from Slack or your phone. When it needs you, it's one tab away.

Download Orca  ·  Explore bots →

## Features
### Orca Bots Ask a bot in Slack, Linear, or GitHub to fix a bug, and come back to a tested pull request. It runs on your own Claude Code or Codex. Open its work in Orca to review it or step in. [Overview](https://orca.dev/bots) · [Security](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/bots)
### Chat or Terminal Run any agent in Chat UI or as the raw CLI, and move a conversation between the two without losing context. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/native-chat)
### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)
### Mobile App Pair Orca with the mobile app to get pinged when an agent needs you, reply in chat, and keep work moving on any of your machines when you are away from your desk. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Android APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Review AI Output Review diffs, leave notes on exact changed lines, and send focused feedback back to an agent. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Git Integration Draft commit messages and pull requests from the diff, then send failing checks or PR review comments back to an agent to fix. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/commit-push)
### Parallel Worktrees Quickly split tasks into isolated environments, so multiple agents can work side by side without interfering with each other. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Design Mode Click any element in Orca's browser to copy its HTML, styles, and selector, then paste it into your agent's chat. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native See your GitHub and Linear tasks in one place, and start a workspace for each when you're ready to build. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### Orca CLI Anything you can do in Orca, your agents can do too: create worktrees, start workers, drive the browser and desktop apps, and schedule automations, all from the command line. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
### Plugins Themes, editors, languages, and panels from the community, installed in a click. [Browse plugins →](https://orca.dev/plugins)
### Split Anything Put agents, terminals, browsers, and diffs side by side in split panes shaped to the task. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/tabs-panes-splits)
**Also in the box:** - **[Bot Schedules & Triggers](https://orca.dev/docs/bots#put-it-on-a-schedule)**: run a bot every weekday at 9, or when a pull request opens, a check fails, or a webhook fires. - **[Bot Memory in Markdown](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security#what-you-can-review)**: a bot's soul and memory are plain Markdown files (`SOUL.md`, `MEMORY.md`) you can read and edit. - **[Drag Files to Agents](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)**: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt. - **[Jump Anywhere](https://orca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)**: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host. - **[Rich Previews](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/viewers)**: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them. - **[Mobile Emulator](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview#mobile-emulator)**: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work. - **[Dictation](https://orca.dev/docs/settings#voice)**: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal. - **[Usage & Accounts](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)**: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out. - **[Automations](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/automations)**: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps. - **[Computer Use](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)**: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers. - **And many, many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

--- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux - **[Download from orca.dev](https://orca.dev/download)** - Or grab a build directly: [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-arm64.dmg) · [macOS Intel](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-x64.dmg) · [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-windows-setup.exe) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-linux.AppImage) · [All builds](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest) _Or via a package manager:_ ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) # Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask. brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Upgrade an existing install brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Release candidates (conflicts with the stable cask; uninstall it first) brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca@rc # Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source yay -S stably-orca-bin ``` ### Mobile App — iOS, Android Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone. - **iOS:** [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) - **Android:** [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Download APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Install guide](https://orca.dev/docs/android-apk) --- ## Community & Support - **Discord:** Join the community on **[Discord](https://discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q)**. - **Twitter / X:** Follow **[@orca_build](https://x.com/orca_build)** for updates and announcements. - **WeChat:** Scan to join an Orca community WeChat group. - **Feedback & Ideas:** We ship fast. Missing something? [Request a new feature](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues). - **Privacy:** See the [privacy & telemetry docs](https://orca.dev/docs/telemetry) for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out. - **Show Support:** [Star](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) this repo to follow along with our daily ships. --- ## Developing Want to contribute or run locally? See our [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.

## Signed Builds Windows code signing sponsored/provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). ## License Orca is free and open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** Source code is MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it under your own branding (see [Trademarks and forks](#trademarks-and-forks)). ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork the source code and build the tool that you want, under your own name and branding. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/00_development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/01_architecture.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License The source code in this repository is licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE). ## Trademarks and forks The MIT license applies **only to the source code**. It does not grant any rights to T3 Tools, Inc.'s trademarks, branding, or trade dress, including the **T3 Code** name, wordmark, logos, and application icons. If you fork, redistribute, or build on T3 Code's source code: - **Use your own branding.** Replace the T3 Code name, wordmark, logos, and application icons in any public fork, redistributed build, website, package, or app store listing. - **Be explicitly clear that your project is unofficial.** Do not use the T3 Code name, wordmark, logo, or branding in your own projects without making it unmistakably clear that your project is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by T3 Tools, Inc. Using our name, wordmark, logo, or branding in a way that suggests official status or affiliation is trademark infringement and unlawful. **Any project indicating or implying that it is an official version of T3 Code when it is not will be pursued to the full extent of the law.** See [TRADEMARK.md](./TRADEMARK.md) for the full trademark and branding policy.

# dsh-our-free-model **简体中文** | [English](README_EN.md)

Trendshift JavaScript 周榜第 1 · 2026-10-05 至 2026-10-11 · 更新中，截至 2026-10-11
> 在 dsh 里装上插件即可使用免费车道，无需登录、注册或填写 API Key。 > > *Install the plugin in dsh to use the free lane without signing in, creating an > account, or entering an API key.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：974582805（OFM技术交流[2群]）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。 - **EAC 渠道**由项目维护者提供。使用兼容宿主时，登录 GitHub 并给本仓库点 Star 即可解锁，无需付费。模型以 EAC 前缀显示，凭据加密保存。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 77 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI、FleetRelay Gateway，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十个账号渠道，一体接入**——LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **视觉特效按需开启**——设置页顶部“视觉特效”开关默认关闭，鱼缸和业务功能始终保留；开启后恢复背景光晕、毛玻璃与装饰动画，选择仅保存在当前浏览器。 - **OFM 插件中心：渠道 / 增强 / 页面统一市场**——新仓库 [Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/ofm-extensions) 承载社区插件：Ed25519 签名索引、安装即校验 SHA-256 与静态扫描、运行在 Worker VM 沙箱（唯一 import 是受控的 `ofm:sdk`，网络只放行 manifest 声明的域名，密钥只进不出，每个 hook 带超时熔断）。渠道插件装上即出现在模型选择器（支持 `replaces` 接管内置车道），增强插件以 插件将已收到的思考作为检查点文本，与原始输入一起发起新请求，要求直接输出整理后的回答。 该机制基于检查点重新发起请求，与上游原生 resume 无关，也不会重放已显示的思考内容。恢复段禁用工具调用；已输出 正文或已开始调用工具的截断回合不执行恢复，以避免内容重复或工具重复执行。 为避免重复长思考，恢复提示要求结论优先、最多 800 词；此为提示层面的约束（非硬性 token 限制），模型可能不遵守。恢复属于降级回答，原始请求中的长篇或逐步分析可能被简化。 每个逻辑回合最多两次物理请求：原始请求加一次恢复。默认总时限 900 秒（15 分钟），恢复段最多 300 秒，且受剩余总时长约束；恢复输出上限 8192 tokens，并继续受用户与模型的上限 约束。首段已知的输出 tokens 会从原始预算中扣除，恢复预算不足 512 tokens 时不发起恢复。 检查点最多 131072 字符，且必须通过基于文本字节的保守上下文余量估算；该估算不计算图片 token，不等同于精确的 tokenizer 校验。超出限制即停止恢复，不会无限续接。恢复必须正常结束且 产生非空白正文方为成功；失败返回 STREAM_CUT，宿主不会将该回合整轮重发，用户取消 则保持 aborted / ABORTED。 可通过本机 settings.json 的 streamRecovery: false 关闭恢复；也可通过对象的 enabled 开关及数值限制收窄边界，数值只能低于或等于默认上限。默认不限制模型名单。 用量看板将物理请求与逻辑回合分开统计。上游请求数与请求失败数按实际发出的请求次数计数； 对话回合数、回合失败数与已恢复数按一次适配器调用的最终结果计数。例如首段中断、 续写成功会记为 2 次上游请求、1 次请求失败，同时记为 1 worker/README.md。 **GitHub 授权闸门**：自建网关（宝塔 Node 形态）另带一道按人计的授权闸门——对话请求除签名外还需携带一枚**专属令牌**，而令牌只发给「用 GitHub 登录 + 已 star 本仓库」的账号。登录全程在浏览器里完成：设置页「EAC 渠道授权」一键发起，网关回调页确认 star 状态后签发令牌，插件自动领取，无需复制粘贴；未 star 时页面会给出 ⭐ 按钮与「我已 star，重新检查」，不必重新登录。网关默认每 12 小时用保存的授权复查一次 star，取消 star 即在复查窗口内吊销令牌；GitHub 侧不可达时保留既有判定，不会误伤已授权用户。网关只申请 `read:user` 最小权限，授权仅用于 star 复查。免费车道（opencode）不经过网关，完全不受影响。 ## 上游是哪些源 两条公开免密来源，均直连、不经任何第三方中转；另有第四条出网目标为自建网关（EAC 渠道，见其专节）。 **免费车道：OpenCode 的免密网关，https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/\***（2026-10-14 从 `/zen/v1` 迁到这里；旧路径对免费模型一律 403 FreeTierError）。 具体到代码——src/upstream.js 中每一条均通过直接请求核对（路径与指纹：2026-10-14 / 10-16）： | 用途 | 目标 | 携带何种凭据 | | --- | --- | --- | | 推理请求 | POST …/inference/v1/chat/completions、…/inference/v1/responses、…/inference/v1/messages（按模型分流，见 endpointFor） | Authorization: Bearer public——该车道本身即为公开免密额度，插件中不含任何属于你的密钥 | | 模型清单 | GET …/inference/v1/models | 同上 | | 公告与升级清单 | 本仓库的 feed/\*.json：raw.githubusercontent.com 优先，cdn.jsdelivr.net 兜底 | 无 | | 出口地区判定 | api.ipify.org / ipinfo.io / ipapi.co，仅用于读取本机公网 IP 与国家码 | 无 | **Kilo 渠道：Kilo AI 的公共网关，https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway**（2026-10-06 接入）。 代码在 src/kilo.js，每一条均于接入当日通过直接请求核对： | 用途 | 目标 | 携带何种凭据 | | --- | --- | --- | | 推理请求 | POST …/api/gateway/chat/completions（OpenAI Chat Completions 兼容，SSE 流式） | **无**——该网关的免费池（清单中 `isFree: true` 的模型，含 kilo-auto/free 自动路由）不需任何账号、Key 或登录态 | | 模型清单 | GET …/api/gateway/models | 无 | 关于隐私与信任，说明如下： 没有号池、没有中转、没有二道贩子。上表即为本插件全部出网目标；npm test 的离线套件完全不出网（共享测试脚手架会把两条免密来源都默认指向已关闭的本机端口，杜绝任何套件"顺带"打到真实网关），仅 scripts/host-selftest.mjs 与 scripts/probes/ 会主动请求这些地址，且需手动运行。若将来引入新的来源，本节会先于功能更新，不会默认将流量分配给第三方。 你的 prompt、工具结果与随附图像会作为正常推理请求发送至所选模型对应的上游——与调用任何模型 API 相同。除此之外插件不上传任何内容：用量看板数据、设置、转发 Key 均只落在本机 DSH_HOME/our-free-model/。 免密不等于无人管理：免费车道通过 x-opencode-\* 指纹识别客户端、按会话统计免费额度，会因地区返回 403、因超量返回 429。**Kilo 免费池在其模型卡中明确声明：prompt 可能被上游提供方记录，并用于改进其服务**（原文见 kilo-auto/free 模型卡："Prompts may be logged by the upstream provider and used to improve their services. Not suitable for production or sensitive data workloads."）。模型集合与额度政策由上游决定，随时可能变更；插件仅能如实将不可用的模型从选择器中移除。 本节属于仓库文档。应用内的选择器、设置页与报错文案中仍不出现上游厂名（该约定见验收情况一节），但 Kilo 渠道的模型卡徽章悬停提示会告知"prompt 可能被上游记录"——这是选择模型时需要知道的信息。 ## 免责声明 - **本插件是一个客户端，不是模型服务方。** 所有模型响应均由上述第三方上游（OpenCode Zen 网关、Kilo AI 公共网关、以及你自己部署的 EAC 网关）生成并传输；插件不托管、不修改、不过滤任何模型输出。模型可能产出错误、过时或有偏颇的内容，请自行核实后再使用。 - **免费不等于无限，也不等于私有。** 免费额度由上游单方面提供，随时可能限流、收费或下线；Kilo 免费池明确声明 prompt 可能被上游记录并用于改进服务。**请勿通过本插件的免费车道发送密码、密钥、个人身份信息、商业机密或任何你不愿第三方处理的内容**；生产与敏感场景请使用你自己的付费 API。 - **上游条款由你遵守。** 使用各渠道即表示你同意对应上游的服务条款与用量政策；因违反上游政策导致的限流、封禁或其它后果由使用者自行承担。插件不对任何上游的可用性、准确性或连续性作任何承诺。 - **EAC 渠道仅限通过 GitHub 授权的用户使用。** 网关由项目维护者部署，登录 GitHub 并给本仓库点 Star 即可解锁，无需付费；请勿尝试绕过授权闸门，勿转售或共享渠道访问权——滥用会导致全体用户的通道被收紧。 - **本插件与上述任何上游厂商无隶属或背书关系。** 各厂商名称与商标归其各自所有者所有，仅在说明来源时引用。 ## 安全与隐私 所有状态写入 DSH_HOME/our-free-model/；用量与设置仅落在本机，不上传至任何位置。 聚合车道的 Key 同样不出本机：它只写入插件自己的 0600 `settings.json`，请求只发往你自己配置的那家提供商，插件接口只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹，从不回显 Key 本身；测试与发现模型两次探测也把回包中的 Key 一律脱敏。 转发监听仅绑定回环地址，默认 127.0.0.1，无 Key 请求一律拒绝。将地址改为可路由接口会被直接拒绝（POST /settings 返回 400 并注明原因；在无 web server 的 composition 中手工写入 settings.json 同样不会启动监听）——该端口的流量消耗的是本机这条免密车道，不应由一个字符串决定是否向整个子网开放。 局域网访问是另开的一扇门，并不放宽上述规则：本机监听仍只绑回环、修改地址仍被拒绝；需要跨机器使用时必须显式启用"局域网访问"，中继绑定可路由地址，且每个请求都需携带局域网 Key——连 /、/health 这类存活探针也一并鉴权（仅本机监听免 Key 应答存活探测），否则一个未鉴权的应答等同于向整个子网宣告"该主机正在代理"。中继仅转发 /v1/models、/v1/chat/completions、/v1/responses、/v1/messages、/v1/messages/count_tokens 五条白名单路径（各自的去 /v1 写法同样放行），不代理任意 loopback 服务；入口处将局域网 Key 换为本机 Key，因此两把 Key 互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。本仓库不含任何硬编码凭据。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经 dns.lookup 解析、全部结果均为回环才放行，绑定使用解析出的 IP——当 hosts 文件或企业 DNS 将 localhost 指向可路由接口时，校验与监听不再各自为政。 卸载只需移除 bundle 条目，插件不留任何补丁；其数据目录为纯 JSON，可直接删除。 ## 许可证 本仓库自己的代码是 MIT，见 LICENSE。第三方组件和数据的许可证见下一节「致谢」。 本项目为独立插件，与任何模型提供方无隶属、认可或赞助关系。使用该插件访问免费额度受各提供方 自身条款约束；在超出个人机器的场景中部署前，请先确认这些条款。 ## 致谢 感谢 Jet（iJetLi）的渠道包（`vendor/channel-pack/`，MIT；上游仓库 [dsh-providers-hub](https://github.com/iJetLi/dsh-providers-hub)）—— 十个内置账号渠道的登录、账号池与本地网关都出自这里，许可证与出处见该目录下的 LICENSE 与 NOTICE.md。 也感谢这些项目： - [models.dev](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev)（MIT）：模型窗口、输出上限与思考档位。目录数据按 MIT 使用，许可证全文见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 - [9router](https://github.com/decolua/9router)（MIT）：`scripts/probes/` 下 8 个取证脚本的原始来源——那 8 个文件是逐字副本（只改了探测的 base URL），文件头保留了 MIT 归属，许可证全文见 [LICENSE](LICENSE#9router--mit)。它们 import 9router 自己的模块，只在该项目的 checkout 内可运行，不进发行集。 - [magpie-muse-web](https://github.com/JohnWangggg/magpie-muse-web)（上游未声明 SPDX 许可证）：`muse-web` 桥接扩展的上游。 **以下项目在本仓库里不再有任何代码或数据**，只作为历史记录保留： - [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)（GPL-3.0）：免费车道请求整形的最早参考。2.8.6 已把相关实现重写并删除其资产，当前代码与该项目的文件没有共享文本、函数名或常量表；现在只按 [sst/opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) v2.2.3（MIT）生成的官方资产工作，见 [维护说明](src/o2a/SYNC.md)。 - [free-claude-code](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code)（AGPL-3.0-only）：供应商目录与五个本地应答的最早参考。2.8.6 重写本地应答、按 models.dev 重建目录；只剩五个优化 id 与部分 provider id 作为**持久化配置键**沿用（改名会让用户已关掉的开关静默复活），见 [兼容说明](docs/provider-compatibility.md)。 - [trae-mate](https://github.com/luckymiaow/trae-mate)（MIT）：TRAE 签到流程的早期参考，已被重写取代。 - [dsh-cline-pass](https://github.com/codeOct/dsh-cline-pass)（MIT）：Cline 额度与请求记录的早期参考，已被重写取代。 - [rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk)（CLI Apache-2.0，engine BUSL-1.1）：工具输出过滤器的最早参考。`src/token-saver/compact/` 已全部重写，仅保留 RTK 的输出标记与阈值——那些标记是模型读惯的线格式，改掉会改变模型行为而不是让代码更原创。2.8.6 的替换范围见 [验证记录](docs/verification/2026-11-18-independent-core.md)。 根目录的 MIT 只覆盖 OFM 自己写的代码；上面仍在使用的组件和数据按各自许可证提供，完整条款以上游 LICENSE 为准。这份名单是来源记录，不改变任何组件的许可证。 ## Star 趋势 图表由 Star History 自动更新，无需手动提交图片。受服务缓存（当前为 24 小时）和 GitHub 图片缓存影响，显示可能延迟，并非秒级实时；点击图表可查看在线趋势。

items.readme_text:
![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **85 skills** · 16 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY

      

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 85 skills + 16 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 85 skills + 16 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **85 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 7 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 5 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **16 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — `triage-validation`'s 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The `bugcrowd-reporting` skill includes researcher-side hygiene (Bugcrowdninja alias, account-state restoration, friendly-tester posture) that signals legitimate authorized testing to the target's fraud team. The bundle explicitly **excludes**: weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full posture. > **Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards.** Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that **block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default** — so even *authorized, in-scope* work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's **free, application-based [Cyber Verification Program (CVP)](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case)** to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are *not* adjustable.) Details: [Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude). ### Why your model switched mid-session Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On **Opus 5**, a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names *exploit generation*, *binary-based vulnerability scanning* and *penetration testing* — **fall back to Opus 4.8** rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See [why Claude switched models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5). What to do depends on what you are actually doing: | Situation | What helps | |---|---| | **Auditing your own code** — reviewing a repo you own for defects | Say so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive. | | **Authorized offensive work** — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submission | This is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is [CVP](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case). Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead. | | **You just want the switching off** | Settings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching. | `/hunt` states the engagement frame (authorized, scope-bounded, remediable finding) on its first turn for exactly this reason — engagement context belongs in the session explicitly, not implied. --- ## Documentation | Doc | Contents | |---|---| | [`README.md`](README.md) | This file — overview, quickstart, scope, skill summary | | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) | Full setup with Burp MCP integration and optional skill regenerator | | [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) | Workflow walkthrough · decision tree · worked engagement example | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | 6-phase architecture · skill-to-phase mapping · engagement composition | | [`docs/cbh-cli.md`](docs/cbh-cli.md) | `cbh` CLI — native runner orchestrating recon + classify + triage + report | | [`docs/cve-coverage.md`](docs/cve-coverage.md) | CISA KEV coverage snapshot — refreshed weekly via the workflow template at `docs/automation/cve-refresh.yml.template` | | [`docs/credits.md`](docs/credits.md) | Full attribution: 43 original skills + 8 vendored from upstream | | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) | PR guidelines · skill quality standards · scope | | [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | Authorized-use posture · responsible disclosure · what's excluded | | [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) | MIT | | [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) | Upstream-skills attribution · no-redistribution note | | [`LICENSE-CONTENT`](LICENSE-CONTENT) | CC BY 4.0 (skill methodology, wordlists, docs) | --- ## Why this exists Most bug-hunting Claude setups are either too generic (one big "security" prompt) or too fragmented (you bookmark 30 disclosed reports and re-read them every engagement). Neither scales past the second target. This bundle was built and validated through authorized engagements that exposed different capability gaps: **Bug-bounty engagement** — surfaced four gaps a starter 3-skill stack could not close: 1. **No hypothesis discipline** — drafts written before validation → wasted hours, hurt validity ratio 2. **No per-program reporting tactics** — VRT defaults auto-downgraded P3-worthy findings to P4 3. **No engagement coordination** — findings, evidence, and submission IDs scattered across folders 4. **No evidence hygiene** — screenshots leaked cookies and victim PII **External red-team engagement** — exposed five additional gaps that bug-bounty defaults made worse: 1. **Conservative defaults retracted real findings** — WAPT mindset stopped tests early on defended targets where red-team continuation would have surfaced bypass chains → `redteam-mindset` 2. **No mid-engagement situational awareness** — client SOC patched confirmed SQLi within 30 min; external attacker locked 14 accounts during a live test session — both invisible without explicit detection methodology → `mid-engagement-ir-detection` 3. **No enterprise-platform attack chains** — M365 + Entra ID, on-prem SharePoint, Cisco SSL VPN, vCenter, and 7 Android APKs all needed current 2024-2026 CVE knowledge and platform-specific tradecraft → `m365-entra-attack`, `okta-attack`, `hunt-sharepoint`, `hunt-aspnet`, `hunt-ntlm-info`, `vmware-vcenter-attack`, `enterprise-vpn-attack`, `apk-redteam-pipeline` 4. **No client-facing deliverable format** — bug-bounty report templates don't fit enterprise red-team where output is a 50KB+ MD + DOCX with embedded screenshots → `redteam-report-template` 5. **No post-credential escalation model** — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate → `cloud-iam-deep` The per-class `hunt-*` skills address gap-zero (*"what should I look for in webapps"*) — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. The enterprise-platform and red-team-tradecraft layers address what bug-bounty alone cannot: external red-team engagements against monitored enterprise targets. --- ## Roadmap - [x] HackerOne MCP integration — [`mcp/hackerone/`](mcp/hackerone/README.md): disclosed-report duplicate search, program stats and scope; optional logged-in mode for private programs and your own reports - [ ] Per-engagement memory layer — pattern recall across targets - [x] Industry-specific hunt skills — `hunt-fintech-graphql` shipped; `hunt-healthcare-fhir`, `hunt-gov-compliance` still open - [x] Program-scope importer — `cbh scope import` builds `scope.md` from a program's published scope (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack via [bounty-targets-data](https://github.com/arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data); HackerOne MCP output for private programs; or pasted program text), failing closed on anything ambiguous — see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) - [ ] Refresh `hunt-*` skills with newer disclosed reports (re-run `public-skills-builder`) - [ ] Additional enterprise-platform skills — `citrix-netscaler-deep`, `f5-bigip-attack`, `ad-cs-attack` (AD Certificate Services) - [ ] Refresh enterprise-VPN CVE matrix quarterly to track 2026 advisories - [ ] Update architecture SVG to include the 7-skill enterprise-platform layer --- ## Sponsors

**[ApiSmart](https://www.apismart.ai/)** unifies leading LLM, image, and video models through one OpenAI-compatible API. Use one key to switch models, simplify billing, and improve reliability with automatic failover.

**[ThreatWatch360](https://threatwatch360.com)** is an AI-powered offensive-security platform: continuous Attack Surface Management, AI-assisted penetration testing, brand protection, dark-web monitoring, and Cyber Threat Intelligence in one platform. Validated findings with proof-of-concept and business-impact prioritization — signal over alert fatigue. --- ## About Operational tradecraft accumulated across bug-bounty engagements and authorized pentests, codified into Claude skills. Platform-agnostic — slot into any engagement workflow you already use, or none. **Author:** [ElementalSoul](https://github.com/elementalsouls) · GenAI Security Research **Sister project:** [Claude-OSINT](https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-OSINT) — paired skills for the recon phase that this bundle picks up after. Its two recon skills (`offensive-osint`, `osint-methodology`) are **canonically maintained here** and re-exported there, so the two are byte-identical. **Installing both is safe:** each bundle's installer (`install.sh` on macOS/Linux, `install.ps1` on Windows) records a manifest, the script skips re-copying an identical skill, and `--uninstall` keeps any skill the other bundle still owns — uninstalling one never breaks the other. **Vendored foundation:** [shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty](https://github.com/shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty) — methodology, validation, reporting, payload library (8 of 85 skills + 16 slash commands) **Generator tool used (not vendored):** [shuvonsec/public-skills-builder](https://github.com/shuvonsec/public-skills-builder) — used to scaffold per-class skills from H1 disclosed reports **Inspirations:** - [archangel / douglasday](https://hackerone.com/) — top-10 H1 hunter; per-class skill pattern - [Trail of Bits — `trailofbits/skills`](https://github.com/trailofbits/skills) — skill-authoring discipline - [SecSkills — `trilwu/secskills`](https://github.com/trilwu/secskills) — subagent pattern **Tool inventory:** - [PortSwigger Burp Suite + MCP Server extension](https://portswigger.net/burp) - [ProjectDiscovery](https://github.com/projectdiscovery) — subfinder · dnsx · httpx · katana · nuclei - [SecLists](https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists) · [Assetnote Wordlists](https://wordlists.assetnote.io/) ## License This project is dual-licensed: - **Code** (Python helpers, shell scripts) — [MIT](LICENSE). - **Content** (skill methodology, wordlists, regex catalogs, severity rubrics, docs) — [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](LICENSE-CONTENT) (CC BY 4.0). # ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20server-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/VKyvMTcgXh) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md) [![Join us on Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/JOIN%20US%20ON-DISCORD-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/VKyvMTcgXh)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup: ```bash docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token" ``` > Multi-arch release images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) are published to GitHub Container > Registry at `ghcr.io/baarai/artex` from the next tagged release; v0.7.0 predates the publish > step. For pulling the prebuilt image and all other installation paths (script, binaries, > source, release archives), see [Installation](#installation). --- ## Multi-provider workers In **System → LLM**, configure the profiles you want to use. In **System → Settings**, set the concurrent worker count to at least **2** before starting a task (the count applies to subsequently started tasks). In **System → Agents → Worker**, leave the model set to follow the task; a fixed Worker model takes precedence over rotation. When creating a task, select both profiles in **LLM config chain**, arrange their order, and enable **Enable multi-LLM worker rotation**. For an existing task, open its LLM config control, change the switch or profile order, and save. Rotation assigns successive worker intents A, B, A, B, regardless of completion order. Separate intents can run concurrently on different providers; each intent keeps its selected provider unless it fails over. Planner and other unbound roles continue using the task's current profile. Turning rotation off restores ordered task-level failover. An excluded provider is skipped, so an intent pinned to an exhausted profile falls back to the task's current profile instead of retrying it; rotation keeps cycling the whole list and does not rebalance around a dead provider. Saving the chain resets their failure state. Changes do not interrupt in-flight calls. The rotation cursor starts again after a server restart and saving the chain does not reset it; the profile order and switch remain persisted. The task creation and `PUT /api/tasks/{id}/llm` APIs accept `llm_rotate: true` alongside the ordered `llm_profile_ids`. Omitting `llm_rotate` on an update preserves its value. ## Screenshots | Tasks | Findings | | :---: | :---: | | ![Tasks](screenshots/tasks.png) | ![Findings](screenshots/findings.png) | | Task execution: sessions and tool calls | Exploration graph | | :---: | :---: | | ![Execution](screenshots/sessions.png) | ![Exploration graph](screenshots/graph.png) | | Asset coverage graph | Traffic recording | | :---: | :---: | | ![Asset coverage graph](screenshots/assets_test.png) | ![Traffic](screenshots/traffic.png) | | Human-in-the-loop chat | Interception approvals | | :---: | :---: | | ![Chat](screenshots/chat.png) | ![Interception](screenshots/intercept.png) |
More screenshots (assets, agents, LLM, logs) | Assets | Agent management | | :---: | :---: | | ![Assets](screenshots/assets.png) | ![Agent](screenshots/agents.png) | | LLM configuration | Backend logs | | :---: | :---: | | ![LLM](screenshots/llm.png) | ![Logs](screenshots/logs.png) |
--- ## How it works ### Dual-graph architecture: exploration graph + asset graph ARTEX separates *what the goals are* from *how far testing has progressed* into two independent graphs linked by anchors: - **Asset graph (shared across tasks).** One source of truth for `root_domain / subdomain / ip / service / app / endpoint`, owned by companies. Parent-child relationships and deduplication keys are computed by the program; agents only submit raw observations. - **Exploration graph (per task).** The task's reasoning and progress: `goal / intent / fact / finding / hint` nodes connected by `spawns / derived_from / yields / proves` edges into a lineage chain. - **Anchors link them.** `exploration_anchors(node_id, asset_id)` ties intents, facts and findings to concrete assets: which assets a direction touched, and which intents tested a given asset. This also powers **asset test coverage** and the coverage graph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EG["Exploration graph (per-task · advance chain)"] direction TB G["goal"] I1["intent A"] F1["fact"] I2["intent B"] FD["finding (vulnerability)"] G -->|spawns| I1 I1 -->|yields| F1 F1 -->|derived_from| I2 I2 -->|proves| FD end subgraph AG["Asset graph (globally shared · source of truth)"] direction TB RD["root_domain"] SD["subdomain"] SV["service"] EP["endpoint"] RD --> SD --> SV --> EP end I1 -. anchor .-> SD F1 -. anchor .-> SV I2 -. anchor .-> EP FD -. anchor .-> EP ``` The **planner** reads the exploration graph, judges goals, and dispatches intents only when there is an uncovered direction; a **worker** claims one intent, executes it, writes assets/facts/findings back into both graphs, then stops. ### The engine loop The engine is event-driven: any graph change wakes the planner, workers claim and execute intents, write-back triggers the next round, until `prove_goal` closes the task. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant EV as graph-change debounce participant P as planner participant FR as frontier intent queue participant W as worker participant PX as recording proxy participant DB as dual graphs + activity EV-->>P: wake up P->>DB: read situation (graph_overview prefetch + coverage/scope) P->>FR: dispatch 0..N intents (with asset_ids) Note over P,FR: most wake-ups dispatch 0 (no new direction means done) W->>FR: claimNext claims one intent W->>DB: fetch the raw assets of the intent's asset_ids W->>PX: real tool execution (Kali / Bash / HTTP) PX-->>W: response (fully traced + CA verified) W->>DB: write back fact / asset / finding + per-step activity DB-->>EV: graph change EV-->>P: wake again (closed loop) ``` ### Durable attack chains, shared worker memory Real attack chains are multi-step and ordered (find an injection → get credentials → move laterally). The planner keeps a **todolist retained per task across wake-ups**: it records the chain once, then dispatches the next step only when its prerequisites are satisfied by facts. Workers can also **search each other's execution traces** (`search_all_worker_traces`, `list_worker_traces`, `get_worker_trace`). Observations that never became formal facts (an error message, a response snippet, a hidden parameter) are still reusable by the next worker, while each worker remains confined to the intent it claimed. --- ## Features ### Evidence, not chat logs - **Recording MITM proxy** (`:8788`) with a generated CA: every Bash/HTTP tool call is traced, and request/response evidence can be bound to a finding. - **Browser extension** (`extension/`) for authenticated targets: log in once (captcha, email OTP, 2FA included), capture the session, and the requests/responses land in the same traffic store.
Using the traffic capture extension - Load the unpacked extension from `extension/` (Chrome/Edge: Developer Mode → Load unpacked); - In the popup, set your ARTEX URL and token, then press **Start capture** on the tab you are browsing; - Use the site normally; text requests/responses are batched to `POST /api/traffic/ingest` (authenticated). Binary bodies (images, fonts) are skipped, bodies are truncated at 256 KiB, batches are capped at 50 entries; - Press **Stop** when done. Everything stays in your local traffic store.
- **Verified findings**: findings carry a POE level, a verification status and a note; a finding is `verified` only when a bound proof/response and verbatim evidence quotes support it. Gzip/deflate bodies are decoded before the quote check. The findings table supports bulk status updates, and the report and export show each finding's proof strength next to its status. - **Traffic replay**: open a captured exchange and replay the recorded request (method, URL, headers and stored body) from the traffic detail; replay stays disabled while only the body preview is loaded. - **Vulnerability retest loop**: a dedicated `retester` agent re-runs a finding with optional fixed version/conditions, records `Still reproducible / Fixed / Cannot confirm`, and can move the finding to `Fixed` automatically. Original evidence and reports are preserved. - **Reports and exports**: findings, evidence and task archives, with traffic snapshots kept encrypted at rest. ### Control without slowing down - **Interception gate**: every tool call can require human approval, with rules by `string`, `regex` or **argv prefix**. An argv rule is a JSON array of 1 to 8 tokens (Bash only, for example `["git","push"]`); it matches only a single simple command whose parsed prefix equals the pattern exactly. Pipes, lists, redirections, prefix assignments, subshells, background jobs, wrapper programs and command/parameter substitutions do not match; flags are ignored by construction (`["git","push"]` covers `git push --force`, but `git -C /repo push` matches nothing). Each approval records who decided: `human`, `rule`, `model` or `system`. - **Scope and target gate**: scope rows define the coverage denominator; assets outside the declared scope are not explored. The target gate (off by default, API-only) can refuse destinations that were not approved. - **Budgets**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a whole task (planner and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Near the limit the task enters a forced wrap-up; a worker is not started when the remaining budget cannot cover it. Spend already in `llm_usage` is restored after a restart. A task that is already inside the wrap-up reserve only has that reserve left, so the revived run wraps up instead of starting another worker. The per-worker cost estimate starts again from the defaults (50,000 tokens and 10 turns) until a worker finishes in this process. - **Noise governor**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE=quiet|balanced|aggressive` paces requests ARTEX sends to targets (per-host rate, burst, in-flight limit, jitter, backoff on 429/503, short GET caching). With a profile set, agents also receive low-and-slow flags for the installed scanners. - **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Disable with `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0`. ### Assets and coverage - **Coverage ledger and force-directed coverage graph**: in-scope assets are highlighted as tested or untested, with linked intents, facts and findings per node. - **Company-scoped asset graph**: shared across tasks, deduplicated by the program, with domain → subdomain → service → endpoint containment. - **ScopeSentry sync**: pull asset data from a [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) instance by project or task, merged by company scope into the asset graph for agents to explore.

See [Task archive storage](docs/task-archive-storage.md) for configuration, permissions, integrity checks, temporary disk requirements and recovery. **Concurrency**: work agents per task, in "System Settings" (default 3). **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results for the worker, planner, chat and main agent are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Unset or empty, the boundary is on; set `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0` (or `false` / `off` / `no`) to disable it. Cost: about 154 bytes per tool result plus one system note. **Noise profile (off by default)**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE` paces the requests ARTEX sends to targets (WebFetch, HTTP custom tools, the enrich probe). Unset or `off` keeps today's behaviour: no limit, no cache. `quiet` = 2 req/s per host (burst 4, 1 in flight), `balanced` = 5 req/s (burst 10, 2 in flight), `aggressive` = 20 req/s (burst 40, 4 in flight). A profile adds jitter, backs off on 429/503 (honours `Retry-After`, bounded retries, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), deduplicates identical in-flight GETs and caches them briefly (60/30/10 s; never POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and logs a per-host noise line each minute. `ARTEX_TARGET_USER_AGENT` sets a User-Agent on target requests that carry none. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests) are paced too, per host by the same rate and jitter, and counted in the same per-host lines. The in-flight caps, retries and cache apply only to ARTEX's own requests. This is best effort, not a security boundary. Raw scanners such as nmap are not paced, and neither is a command that bypasses the proxy (`--noproxy`, a removed proxy variable). With capture off, nothing launched from Bash is paced. The low-and-slow prompt block supplies the rate flags in every case. The **Target noise** card in System settings sets the profile at runtime (no restart) and shows the per-host counters; once saved, that setting takes precedence over `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE`. **Scanner User-Agent (opt-in per task)** adds a stable ARTEX User-Agent to supported target requests so defenders can correlate them with an approved assessment. See the [configuration and WAF triage guide](docs/scanner-user-agent.md). **Low-and-slow agent guidance (off by default)**: when a noise profile is set, the planner, worker, main agent and chat agents receive a code-owned prompt block with the profile's per-host limits and exact rate/delay flags for the installed scanners. It tells them to test one host at a time, back off on 429/503 and never raise the rate to meet a deadline. **Run budgets (off by default)**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a task's total spend (planner rounds and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Unset or `0` means unlimited. A worker is not started when the remaining task budget cannot cover its estimated cost (the average of finished workers, else 50,000 tokens and 10 turns). Near the wrap-up reserve (the larger of 5% and 20,000 tokens, and 2 turns) the task enters a forced wrap-up: the planner writes a summary and final goal judgment, and workers may only write back. The task then ends `done` if its goals are met, else `timeout`. Practical floor: below 50,000 tokens no worker starts; 50,000-70,000 typically gives one worker then wrap-up; pick well above 70,000 for real exploration. Planner, worker, judge, and compactor rows in `llm_usage` are counted back into the cap when a ledger is created, including after a restart and after a revived run drops its ledger. A restored task already inside the wrap-up reserve does not get another worker: only that reserve remains, and the run wraps up. Chat, goal decomposition, and side questions are stored on the same task and are not counted. The per-worker average is not restored (usage rows have no run boundary), so the estimate starts from the defaults until a worker finishes in this process. **Common flags**: `./start.sh -addr :8787 -proxy :8788` (`-addr` frontend/API, `-proxy` traffic recording proxy). ### External PostgreSQL ARTEX already supports an external PostgreSQL 16+ instance — the `postgres` service in `docker-compose.yml` is only the bundled default. Because the database is startup configuration and the system's single source of truth, there is no runtime database switcher in the UI: change the environment variables and restart the server to point at another instance. Configure the connection with either a full connection string or individual parts: - **`ARTEX_PG_DSN`**: full PostgreSQL connection URL (for example `postgres://artex:pass@db.example.internal:5432/artex?sslmode=require`). When set, it takes precedence over the `ARTEX_PG_*` variables and you are responsible for percent-encoding any URL-special characters in the username or password. - **`ARTEX_PG_*` parts** (recommended when passwords contain `/`, `?`, `%`, `@`, `:`, or spaces — ARTEX percent-encodes the user and password and removes `ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD` from the environment at startup): - `ARTEX_PG_HOST` — PostgreSQL host - `ARTEX_PG_PORT` — PostgreSQL port (default `5432`) - `ARTEX_PG_USER` — database user - `ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD` — database password (raw, not URL-encoded) - `ARTEX_PG_DBNAME` — database name - `ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE` — TLS mode (`disable`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`) #### Compose without the bundled `postgres` service To run ARTEX against an external PostgreSQL server with Docker Compose, remove the `postgres` service, the `depends_on` block, and the `pgdata` volume from `docker-compose.yml`, and point `artex` at your database: ```yaml services: artex: image: ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest security_opt: - "no-new-privileges:true" environment: # Option A: individual parts (recommended; percent-encodes special characters) ARTEX_PG_HOST: ${ARTEX_PG_HOST:?Set ARTEX_PG_HOST in .env} ARTEX_PG_PORT: ${ARTEX_PG_PORT:-5432} ARTEX_PG_USER: ${ARTEX_PG_USER:-artex} ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD: ${ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD:?Set ARTEX_PG_PASSWORD in .env} ARTEX_PG_DBNAME: ${ARTEX_PG_DBNAME:-artex} ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE: ${ARTEX_PG_SSLMODE:-require} # Option B: full DSN (overrides ARTEX_PG_* when set) # ARTEX_PG_DSN: ${ARTEX_PG_DSN} ARTEX_JWT_KEY_DIR: /app/keys ports: - "${ARTEX_BIND_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:8787:8787" - "127.0.0.1:8788:8788" volumes: - ./data:/app/data - ./keys:/app/keys restart: unless-stopped ``` #### Local disk usage (`data/`) Moving PostgreSQL to an external host does **not** move the runtime `data/` directory off local disk. `data/` still stores spilled HTTP/TCP traffic blobs (`data/traffic/_blobs`), LLM transcripts, task working files, and local task archives, so heavy workloads can still fill the host disk if `data/` is on a small volume. Mount `data/` on a suitably sized volume, and consider setting `ARTEX_ARCHIVE_STORAGE=s3` (see [Task archive storage](docs/task-archive-storage.md)) to offload cold task archives to object storage. ### Reverse proxy deployment (HTTPS / exposing only 443) The frontend, API and SSE stream share port 8787 (the binary listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default; the Docker container publishes on `127.0.0.1`), and the activity stream is same-origin by default, so **no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` is needed**: expose 443 and keep 8787 internal. SSE keeps a long-lived connection with continuous pushes, so the proxy **must disable buffering**; otherwise the browser connects but never receives events. Redirect plain HTTP first, so a bookmarked `http://` URL never reaches the app unencrypted: ```nginx server { listen 80; server_name your.domain.com; return 301 https://$host$request_uri; } ``` Then the TLS server: ```nginx server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ... location / { # 512 MiB combined file limit plus 1 MiB of multipart metadata. client_max_body_size 513m; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; # SSE essentials: buffering off, long timeouts, HTTP/1.1 proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; } } ``` **Login rate limit behind a proxy**: login allows 10 attempts per minute per client IP. Behind a proxy every request comes from the proxy's address, so without further setup all users share one budget and an attacker who fails 10 logins blocks everyone, admin included, for up to 15 minutes. Keep the `X-Forwarded-For` line and set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated CIDRs, empty by default) to the address ARTEX sees the proxy connect from: - **nginx and ARTEX both on the host** (binary, `./start.sh`): the peer is `127.0.0.1`; start ARTEX with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32`. - **nginx on the host, ARTEX in Docker** (`docker-compose.yml`): the connection reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway (a `172.x` address), not from `127.0.0.1`. Find it with `docker network inspect artex_default --format '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` (the network is `_default`), put `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=/32` in `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`. For a peer in that list, ARTEX reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right and takes the first address that is not a trusted proxy; from any other peer the header is ignored. Trust only proxies you run: a trusted peer can claim any client address. **Security headers**: every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a same-origin referrer policy and a `frame-ancestors 'self'` CSP; console documents additionally get a `Permissions-Policy` and COOP/CORP. `Strict-Transport-Security` is sent only when the request is known to be HTTPS: directly over TLS, or via `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` from a trusted proxy. The same list above enables it, so with nginx in front, the 443 server answers with HSTS after you set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES`. > Only when SSE needs a different origin from the page (e.g. a dedicated subdomain) should you set > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` **at build time** (it is baked into the static bundle during `next build`; > setting it at container runtime has no effect). --- ## Operations ### Troubleshooting an empty tool call In the task's session transcript, expand the affected tool call and compare **Command** and **Output**. The `UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT` markers identify the boundary around tool output. They are expected and should stay enabled while troubleshooting. - **Command shows `{}`.** The recorded tool input is an empty JSON object. For a tool that requires a command, this means its command argument was missing. Check which model and version produced the call. - **Command shows `(empty)` or `(failed to load)`.** The transcript has no input detail to display or could not fetch it. If the session record contains a command, include that discrepancy in a report. - **Output shows `[]`.** This is the recorded result body. Check the row's success or failure indicator and its input separately before drawing conclusions about what ran. For a recurring problem, share the ARTEX version or commit, the model and version, and a sanitized excerpt of the affected input and result. Remove credentials, target data, and other sensitive content before sharing. ### Backups `scripts/backup.sh` dumps the Postgres database (and optionally the data directory) with timestamped output and rotation: ```bash scripts/backup.sh --with-data # db dump + data/ archive, keep 14 scripts/backup.sh --keep 7 # db only, keep 7 ``` Restore into a running stack: ```bash gunzip -c backups/artex-db-.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \ psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" ``` Stored secrets (LLM API keys, proxies and gateway custom headers, MCP env, task credentials, notification channel config, Brave/Tavily search keys, web search and global proxies, the execution spec of custom tools, the capture-proxy rewrite rules) are encrypted in the database with the key in `keys/secret.key` (generated at first start, mode 0600, next to `jwt.key`). **A database backup without that key cannot restore those secrets**: back up `keys/` with the dump, separately. Deployments without a persistent disk set `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64 or hex, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`). ARTEX refuses to start when the database holds encrypted secrets and no key is available. Daily cron example (03:20, operator crontab): ``` 20 3 * * * cd /path/to/ARTEX && scripts/backup.sh --with-data >> backups/backup.log 2>&1 ``` ### Updating and upgrading > Upgrading swaps the program and never touches data: the Postgres volume `pgdata`, `./data` > (traffic index, task files, transcripts), `./keys` (`jwt.key`, `secret.key`) and `./skills` are > preserved. **No manual database step is needed**: on every start ARTEX applies its embedded > `schema.sql` baseline, then any pending numbered migration from `db/migrations/`, in order, each > in its own transaction. Restarting the new binary is the upgrade. Back up `./data`, `keys/` and > the database before upgrading. **Update banner (opt-in, off by default)**: start ARTEX with `ARTEX_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest tag, at most once per 24 hours (cached in memory; a failed check is not retried within that window). When the release is newer, the web UI shows a dismissible strip linking to Releases. The request sends only `User-Agent: artex-update-check`. Unset, ARTEX makes no update request and shows no banner. #### Upgrading from a clone made before 2026-10-23 The repository history was rewritten that day to drop a personal email address from the commit metadata. A clone made before then cannot fast-forward, and `./update.sh` now stops instead of silently rebuilding stale code. Recover once, then upgrade normally: ```bash git stash # only if you have local changes git fetch origin git reset --hard origin/main git stash pop # only if you stashed ``` Your data is unaffected: `./data`, the `pgdata` volume and `./skills` are not part of git history. #### Option 1: one-click update script ```bash cd ARTEX ./update.sh ``` The script optionally `git pull`s, then offers **① Docker update** (`docker compose build artex` → `docker compose up -d artex`) or **② local build update** (rebuild the frontend static assets, then recompile `./artex`; restart the process for it to take effect). #### Option 2: Docker (Compose or GHCR image) ```bash cd ARTEX git pull docker compose build artex docker compose up -d artex docker image prune -f # optional ``` If running the prebuilt `ghcr.io/baarai/artex` container directly, pull the new tag (`docker pull ghcr.io/baarai/artex:latest` or a pinned `:v`) and recreate the container with the same `/app/data` and `/app/keys` mounts. If you run the prebuilt Compose stack, the update is: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml pull docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up -d ``` #### Option 3: prebuilt binaries Download the new zip, stop the old process, overwrite `artex` and `skills/` (keep `config.json` and `data/`), then restart: ```bash cp -r /skills ./ && cp /artex ./ ./start.sh ``` #### Option 4: build from source ```bash git pull cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex # restart ./start.sh ``` --- ## Development ```bash ./dev.sh # backend(:8787) + traffic proxy(:8788) + frontend next dev(:5173) → http://localhost:5173 ``` - Backend: `go run ./cmd/artex` (without `-tags embedui`, the frontend is not embedded) - Frontend: `cd web && npm run dev` (`/api` is reverse-proxied to the backend, with hot reload) - Tests: `go test ./...` - Reproduce the fast CI checks locally: `./scripts/verify.sh` (add `--full` for `-race` and the static web build; add `--security` for `govulncheck`) - Security scan: install `govulncheck` and run `./scripts/verify.sh --security` (CI runs this on every push and pull request) - Mock preview (no backend): `cd web && NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK=1 npm run dev` --- ## Architecture ARTEX is an **LLM multi-agent-driven autonomous penetration testing system**: a Go monolithic backend (with the Next.js UI embedded) + PostgreSQL. Agent capabilities come from the [`norma`](https://github.com/Autumn-27/norma) SDK (`agentcore` / `tool` / `permission` / `harness` / `memory` / `transcript`). At its core is the **dual-graph architecture**, plus two autonomy mechanisms: **process-level information exchange between workers** and the **planner's multi-round shared todolist**. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph FE["Frontend Next.js (go:embed embedded single binary)"] UI["Dashboard · Tasks · Assets · Coverage graph · Traffic · Workspace · System settings"] end subgraph SRV["server (Go net/http)"] API["REST /api/* JWT auth SSE"] ENG["engine scheduling loop"] MGR["Manager task/engine/store lifecycle"] end subgraph AG["agent (norma SDK)"] GO["goals goal decomposition + scope extraction"] PL["planner the planner (sole intent generator)"] WK["worker executor ×N"] MA["mainagent human-in-the-loop"] end subgraph DB["PostgreSQL"] AGRAPH["Asset graph assets / companies / task_scope"] EGRAPH["Exploration graph exploration_nodes / anchors / activity"] end subgraph SUB["Supporting subsystems"] PROXY["Traffic recording proxy MITM + CA tracing"] GUARD["guard / intercept tool approval gate"] ENR["enrich DNS / HTTP async enrichment"] EXT["MCP · skills · memory · report"] end UI -->|HTTP| API API --> MGR --> ENG ENG --> PL ENG --> WK API --> MA API --> GO PL --> DB WK --> DB MA --> DB GO --> DB WK -->|"Bash / HTTP fully traced"| PROXY WK --> GUARD WK --> ENR PL -.-> EXT WK -.-> EXT MA -.-> EXT ``` | Layer | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | **Frontend** | Next.js static export embedded via `go:embed`; tasks, assets, exploration and coverage graphs, traffic, human-in-the-loop chat | | **server** | `net/http` routing, JWT auth, SSE; `Manager` owns tasks, engines and DB stores | | **engine** | One `plannerLoop` + N worker goroutines per task; intent claiming, timeout/pause/drain | | **agent** | goals / planner / worker / mainagent; `ToolSet` exposes the dual graphs as LLM tools | | **db** | PostgreSQL persistence (pgx); embedded schema and numbered migrations applied at startup | | **Supporting** | Recording MITM proxy, approval gate, async enrichment, MCP/skills/memory/report | For the code-level map (execution flow, trust boundaries, decisions) see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md);
